rows: Hetfield purchased the guitar from a mutual member of the schools jazz band.
Purchased for $200 in 1980 and used on Kill 'Em All. Broke in 1984 and restored in 2008.
First used on Ride the Lightning. Also restored in 2008 for the Death Magnetic album.
Jackson King V Custom – "Kill Bon Jovi"
Used during the recording of Master of Puppets and sporadically during the Damage, Inc. Tour in 1986/87.
Hetfield's first ESP and used during the And Justice For All period.
As with his Gibson Explorer – " More Beer ", this was Hetfield's back-up to the ESP MX220 – " Eet Fuk " model.
Hetfield purchased his 3rd ESP in 1988 and while identical to his previous two guitars, this model was all black.
Hetfield used this guitar during live performances of Fade to Black and can be seen during the music video for the song.
Seen during the music video for Nothing Else Matters. Like a stock guitar.
Hetfield used this during the recording of Wherever I May Roam from the Black Album.
Used during the Load period as one of his main live guitars and was painted by artist Dino Muradian.
Custom-made by Ken Lawrence, Hetfield is known to have more than one including a double-neck model.
Designed and built by Matt Masciandaro, Hetfield had two of these guitars. One had red flames, the other one had green.
Essentially a port over from his previous guitars, Hetfield's again had two different versions.
A mid 1990s reissue of the 1952 Fender Telecaster, this guitar was used to record the intro on " The Unforgiven II ".
With artwork designed by Hetfield, all the hardware is gold-plated and the guitar is still used live occasionally.
A gift from Bob Rock, Hetfield used this guitar in the " Turn the Page " music video.
This guitar was used during the St. Anger era, both in the studio as well as on tour.
Also used around the St. Anger period, this guitar was manufactured in 1973.
This guitar was used to record Some Kind of Monster.
Black with green flames, this guitar was used live for songs with Drop D tuning.
Released in 2008, this ESP guitar was another Hetfield signature model.
This guitar has been used live extensively since 2008 and is inspired by his 1973 Gibson Les Paul.
A recent Hetfield addition, it is equipped with a set of James Hetfield signature pickups.
Hetfield has been using this guitar since 2016 and it can be seen on their Instagram and YouTube channels.
